title: Development and prospective evaluation of an oyster-shell-derived amorphous calcium phosphate wet-surface-retentive varnish for root-dentin mineral protection under reduced salivary replenishment: Protocol for a factorial in vitro study
content:
Abstract
Reduced salivary replenishment compromises mineral recovery at exposed root surfaces. Biogenic amorphous calcium phosphate may provide a renewable mineral source, but its phase stability and delivery from a retentive coating require experimental evaluation. Objective: To develop an oyster-shell-derived calcium-phosphate varnish and test root-dentin mineral protection across two controlled artificial-saliva delivery settings. Three traceable shell lots will undergo qualification for contaminants and precursors. Cold-precipitated material will be characterized before a replicated three-by-three screen of mineral and carboxymethyl-chitosan concentrations. A predefined desirability algorithm and non-compensatory phase, processability and extract-safety gates will select one formulation. A separate, assessor-blinded randomized experiment will allocate 144 extracted human teeth to six treatments: no treatment, matched vehicle, selected oyster-derived varnish, synthetic-calcium-phosphate varnish, oyster-derived dispersion and fluoride varnish. Each tooth will provide matched specimens for normal and reduced artificial-saliva replenishment during 14-day non-microbial acid cycling. The primary endpoint is transverse-microradiographic integrated mineral loss in the reduced-replenishment comparison of oyster varnish versus vehicle. Treatment-by-flow interaction and mechanistic outcomes will be secondary. The study will distinguish source-associated and vehicle-associated effects while documenting a transferable development and characterization workflow. The laboratory model will not establish clinical caries-prevention efficacy.
